question: Who lost the 2021 NBA Finals? Show a table.

message.content:

### RELATED: Did the Spurs Exhaust Themselves vs. the Thunder? Wemby Thinks So, and NBA History Agrees

Of those previous 37 teams, only five have come back to win the championship. Three others forced a Game 7 and lost. Since the first edition of the Finals in 1947, it’s been more common for teams facing a 2–0 Finals deficit to get swept (nine times) than to force a Game 7 and/or complete a comeback and hoist the Larry O’Brien Trophy (eight times).

The Spurs don’t have to look too far back in league annals to find an example of a team to overcome it, though. In 2021, Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Bucks trailed the Suns 2–0 after losing the first two games of the Finals by a total of 23 points. Just about every pundit proclaimed the series was over until Antetokounmpo turned things around in Game 3, and the Bucks went on to win the title in six games.

passages.heading: A full list of every team to trail 2–0 in NBA Finals
passages.text:
However, the Spurs face a tougher task ahead than any of those five aforementioned championship-winning teams—the 2021 Bucks, 2016 Cavaliers, 2006 Heat, 1977 Trail Blazers and 1969 Celtics—did when they went down 2–0. All five of those teams lost the first two games of the Finals on the road, and returned to the friendly confines of their home arena for Game 3.

San Antonio, on the other hand, will hit the road and will play Game 3 in front of a rowdy Madison Square Garden crowd that is starving to watch the Knicks win their first title since 1973.

The Spurs are just the third team in history to start the NBA Finals by losing both games at home. The other two teams to do so—the 1995 Magic and 1993 Suns—lost in four and six games, respectively.

The Spurs will have a chance to get their championship dreams back on track when they visit the Knicks at Madison Square Garden in Game 3 on Monday. Tipoff is scheduled for 8:30 p.m. ET.

passages.heading: 2023–24 NBA Finals Champions: Boston Celtics
passages.text:
## 2023–24 NBA Finals Champions: Boston Celtics

After going a league-best 64-18 in the regular season, the Boston Celtics entered the postseason as favorites to win the championship. They lived up to the hype. Boston lost only two games en route to making the NBA Finals, where they faced the Dallas Mavericks. The upstart Mavericks became just the second No. 5 seed to ever make the NBA finals, but the Celtics, led by Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum, proved too much to handle. The Boston Celtics only lost one game to Dallas: Game 4, which the Mavericks won, 122-84. On June 17, 2024, Boston won their NBA-record 18th title with a 106-88 victory in Game 5. Brown was named NBA Finals Most Valuable Player after averaging 20.8 points, 5.4 rebounds and five assists in the series.

passages.heading: 2016–17 NBA Finals Champions: Golden State Warriors
passages.text:
## 2016–17 NBA Finals Champions: Golden State Warriors

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 4–1, to become the 2017 NBA Finals Champions on June 12, 2017, at Oracle Arena in Oakland, California. This was the first NBA Finals to feature the same two teams for the third consecutive year. The Warriors were the first team in the history of the NBA to enter the Finals with a 12–0 playoff record.

sources.title: Spurs must make NBA history to overcome 0-2 deficit vs. Knicks

passages.text:
The San Antonio Spurs must dig themselves out of a massive hole if they’re going to win the NBA Finals after losing Game 2 to the New York Knicks on Friday night.

The Spurs entered Game 2 of the NBA Finals in a must-win situation.

It was bad enough San Antonio allowed the Knicks to keep rolling with a Game 1 win, but the Spurs also allowed New York to wrestle away home-court advantage in the series in a game that saw San Antonio also cough up a 14-point lead.

In Game 2, the Knicks just kept on rolling, winning their 13th-straight game in a 105-104 win over the Spurs in San Antonio.

With the Spurs now down 0-2 against the Knicks, we’re taking a look at the history of teams that have overcome such a deficit in the NBA Finals.

**Spoiler alert:** San Antonio is in big trouble.

passages.heading: History of 0-2 comebacks in NBA Finals
passages.text:
## History of 0-2 comebacks in NBA Finals

Five teams in NBA history have overcome an 0-2 deficit to win the NBA Finals, but NONE of those teams did so after losing the first two games at home.

That means the San Antonio Spurs must make history in order to win the NBA Finals.

The 1969 Boston Celtics (vs. Los Angeles Lakers) and 2016 Cleveland Cavaliers (vs. Golden State Warriors) overcame their 0-2 deficits and won the NBA Finals in seven games.

**MORE: Ticket prices for Game 3 of NBA Finals soar even higher**

The other three teams, the 1977 Portland Trail Blazers (vs. Philadelphia 76ers), the 2006 Miami Heat (vs. Dallas Mavericks) and 2021 Milwaukee Bucks (vs. Phoenix Suns) won in six games.

passages.heading: History of 0-2 comebacks in NBA Finals
passages.text: Outside of the NBA Finals, five teams in league history have overcome an 0-2 deficit in the playoffs after losing two home games to start a series: the 1969 Lakers, the 1994 Houston Rockets, the 2005 Dallas Mavericks, the 2017 Boston Celtics and the 2021 Los Angeles Clippers.

# NBA Champions by Year: Complete list of NBA Finals winners

The __NBA__ Finals are chock-full of history and iconic moments. We've seen legendary franchises, like the Boston Celtics and Los Angeles Lakers, dominate the league, as well as newer powerhouses like the Golden State Warriors and Miami Heat. This year, Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks defeated Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs for their first title in 53 years.

Let's take a look back at the complete list of NBA Finals winners.

passages.heading: **Which teams have won the most NBA championships?**
passages.text:
### **Which teams have won the most NBA championships?**

The Celtics have the most NBA titles with 18. Here’s a list of teams that have won at least three NBA championships:

- Boston Celtics (18 titles)
- Los Angeles Lakers (17)
- Golden State Warriors (7)
- Chicago Bulls (6)
- San Antonio Spurs (5)
- Philadelphia 76ers (3)
- Detroit Pistons (3)
- Miami Heat (3)

passages.heading: **Which teams have never won an NBA championship?**
passages.text:
### **Which teams have never won an NBA championship?**

Ten NBA franchises have never won an NBA Finals:

- Brooklyn Nets
- Charlotte Hornets
- Indiana Pacers
- Los Angeles Clippers
- Memphis Grizzlies
- Minnesota Timberwolves
- New Orleans Pelicans
- Orlando Magic
- Phoenix Suns
- Utah Jazz
